subject: Temporary on-call coverage exception and mitigation plan for LitmusAI
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@litmusai.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary on-call carveout and response SLA for LitmusAI

Hi Redwood support,

We're rolling a major data migration the weekend of Mar 24-26. Our internal ops team will be performing network maintenance that will prevent our outbound connectivity to Redwood's hosted endpoints for an expected 10-hour window each night. Because of that, we're asking for a temporary, documented exception to our P1/P2 response SLA (P1 from 1 hour to 4 hours; P2 from 4 hours to 12 hours) for the maintenance window, plus an agreed escalation path in case of cross-system failures.

We attached a brief request packet (litmus_sla_request_v2.pdf) with the maintenance schedule and a proposed mutual action plan. We're happy to accept mitigation controls—e.g., warm standby on a dedicated pool and explicit on-call escalation contacts—if that helps avoid a formal SLA credit.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can temporarily route LitmusAI traffic to our Dedicated pool and whether you need any additional security/compliance artifacts for the exception? We need a signed amendment by EOD Mar 22 to meet our procurement gating.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform
LitmusAI
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@litmusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary on-call carveout and response SLA for LitmusAI

Daniel — thanks for the packet and the clear timeline. We can support a short, documented SLA deviation provided we implement compensating controls. Narrow summary of what we propose: 

- Temporary SLA change: P1 = 4 hours, P2 = 12 hours (applies to Mar 24 22:00 - Mar 27 08:00 PT nightly windows)
- Mitigation: route traffic to Litmus-dedicated pool (warm standby) + prefix KV caching to limit cross-request state loss
- Escalation path: Litmus ops -> Redwood primary on-call -> Redwood on-call manager (Karthik) -> Redwood incident exec (Marissa)
- Operational artifacts needed: up-to-date on-call roster (attach), signed amendment (DocuSign link below), and one end-to-end canary test prior to the maintenance window

Next steps for our teams:
1) Redwood to confirm dedicated pool availability and cost impact by EOD Tue (Mar 20).
2) Litmus to sign amendment and confirm canary window (we can make a short window Mar 23)
3) Redwood to provide an on-call runbook snippet for the canary and maintenance nights

I'm attaching the current on-call roster (oncall_roster.xlsx) for the team who would be the fallback responders. If you want, I can escalate to Marissa for a faster decision on the duration/cost.

DocuSign (amendment draft): https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123-def

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary on-call carveout and response SLA for LitmusAI

Grace — quick internal note: I'm fine with the proposed mitigations provided we keep the deviation window < 72 hours and require a canary test. Operational considerations:

- Dedicated pool capacity: we can spin up a 2x warm standby for Litmus, cost will be passed through to the customer (estimate attached).
- On-call load: the roster shows two named responders per night; we should add a tertiary responder if we accept the 4-hour P1 SLA, otherwise risk of delayed acknowledgment increases.
- Compliance: Litmus asked for additional artifacts; let's send the SOC2 evidence checklist and limit the amendment to 72 hours to avoid contractual churn.

If Marissa signs off on the 72-hour hard cap we can approve administratively. If they want >72 hours or recurring carveouts, this must go to Legal and Revenue Ops.

-- Karthik
Senior Director, Support Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary on-call carveout and response SLA for LitmusAI

Thanks team — I've reviewed. Approve a one-time, documented SLA exception with the following firm conditions:

- Duration cap: 72 hours max (Mar 24 22:00 through Mar 27 22:00 PT)
- Customer must sign the amendment (DocuSign) before EOD Mar 22
- Litmus to accept a 10% service credit if an incident meets the original P1 criteria during the maintenance window and we fail to meet the interim SLA
- Redwood to run a canary on Mar 23 16:00 PT and confirm warm-standby capacity by Mar 21 EOD

Once executed, please update the HubSpot record and attach the signed amendment. I'm copying Revenue Ops on the credit condition in case billing needs pre-approval.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

-- End of thread --
